s1.quote: 185 feet … definitely for advanced divers … You can penetrate the interior of the ship, but you should do so cautiously

s2.quote: her hulk sunk as an artificial reef off Key West, Florida, 23 November 1983

highlights.text: Upright former salvage ship with penetrable decks

hazards.text: Silt inside the wreck can reduce visibility

s1.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s1.quote: The spurs are ridges of coral 5 to 20 feet deep, with grooves of sandy bottom between cliff-like structures … gentle ledge at about 65 feet, dropping to 90 feet in some places. … ranging from 15 to 110 feet

highlights.text: Spur-and-groove reef beside a 1853 iron lighthouse

hazards.text: Fire coral common on sections of the reef

summary.text: A spur-and-groove reef seven miles off Key West, topped by a historic red iron lighthouse. Coral ridges rise in shallow water and the south side slopes off to a deeper ledge; visibility swings widely with wind and tide.

s1.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s1.quote: ranges in depth from 5 to 35 feet … rubble zone and long fingers of coral with sand and coral-filled canyons

highlights.text: Coral fingers and sand-floored canyons

summary.text: A bank reef off Key West made up of a rubble zone, long coral fingers and sandy, coral-lined canyons, in water shallow enough for relaxed dives.

s1.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s1.quote: ranges in depth from 5 to 35 feet … contains a concentration of important bank reef habitats … rubble zone and long fingers of coral with sand and coral-filled canyons

highlights.text: Coral fingers and sand-floored canyons

summary.text: A small bank reef near Key West packing several reef habitats into about 90 acres, with rubble, coral ridges and sandy canyons in shallow water.

s1.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s1.quote: depths inside the SPA boundaries under 30 feet … classic spur-and-groove reef formation extending over 208 acres in size … one of the most popular sites for snorkeling and diving in the Middle Keys

highlights.text: Classic spur-and-groove reef formation

summary.text: A large spur-and-groove reef in the Middle Keys, shallower than 30 feet inside its protected zone and a favourite for both snorkelers and divers.

s1.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s1.quote: famous for its clear water, fish populations, and numerous boulder corals. It is a classic outer reef with a well-defined spur and groove system … most heavily visited reef in the Upper Keys for scuba diving

s2.quote: One of the most visited reefs in the Upper Keys, Molasses Reef is known for clear water, boulder corals, and abundant marine life.

highlights.text: Boulder corals on a spur-and-groove outer reef
Ship's winch and old Spanish anchor on the bottom

summary.text: Key Largo's busiest outer reef, with spur-and-groove coral, big boulder corals and plentiful fish. Water is often clear, and a winch and an old anchor lie off the lighthouse.

s1.publisher: Islamorada Dive Center
s1.quote: A shallow, protected reef marked by the historic 136-foot Alligator Reef Lighthouse and teeming with marine life across depths of 10 to 25 feet

s2.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s2.quote: some parts of the reef lie at a depth of only 8 feet … a small bank reef protecting a spur-and-groove system … ideal for beginning snorkelers and divers … 632 known species

highlights.text: Historic lighthouse marks the reef
Over 600 reef fish species recorded

summary.text: A shallow protected bank reef off the Alligator lighthouse, with spur-and-groove coral and a big fish list. Calm depths make it a good fit for newer divers and snorkelers.

s1.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s1.quote: half-mile square inshore patch reef … some of the best boulder corals in the Keys as well as star corals and giant brain corals, all in depths of 18 feet or less … Easily accessible by boaters

highlights.text: Boulder, star and giant brain corals

summary.text: A shallow inshore patch reef off Little Palm Island with large boulder, star and brain corals and reef fish, all within 18 feet of the surface.

s1.publisher: Rainbow Reef Dive Center
s1.quote: Site Depth: 15-25 Feet … Site Level: Open Water … One of the largest and healthiest Boulder Brain Corals (Colpophyllia natans) in the Upper Keys can be found on Snapper's Ledge.

s2.quote: A shallow reef averaging around 25 feet, Snapper Ledge is known for schools of yellowtail snapper, nurse sharks, and moray eels.

highlights.text: Huge boulder brain coral
Yellowtail snapper, nurse sharks, morays

summary.text: A shallow Key Largo ledge reef suited to open-water divers, known for a very large boulder brain coral and schools of snapper with nurse sharks and morays around.

sites.name: Duane Wreck

s1.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s1.quote: lies upright on a sandy bottom in 120 feet of water … The mast and crow's nest, protruding high above the hull, are only 60 feet deep. … The superstructure deck is at 90 feet

s2.quote: the Gulf Stream currents that rage so fiercely at times that the site's three mooring buoys are pulled underwater … The Duane makes for an excellent multilevel dive

highlights.text: Intact upright cutter with rails, ladders and props
Multilevel dive from mast down to main deck

hazards.text: Gulf Stream current can be fierce at times

summary.text: A 327-foot Coast Guard cutter sitting upright on sand near Molasses Reef, with the mast near 60 feet and decks stepping down to 120. Currents can run hard, but it makes an easy multilevel wreck dive.

sites.depthNote: Mast 60 ft, bridge 70 ft, main deck 100 ft, sand 120 ft

s1.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s1.quote: lies upright on a sandy bottom in 120 feet of water … The mast and crow's nest, protruding high above the hull, are only 60 feet deep.

s2.quote: the Gulf Stream currents that rage so fiercely at times that the site's three mooring buoys are pulled underwater … The Duane makes for an excellent multilevel dive

summary.text: A decommissioned Coast Guard cutter sunk upright off Key Largo as an artificial reef, with mast and bridge in shallow water and the main deck near 100 feet. Currents can be strong.

s1.publisher: Rainbow Reef Dive Center
s1.quote: Site Depth: 97-130 feet … The currents can make her undiveable at times … Advanced Open Water

s2.quote: the Bibb came to rest on its side … became a much deeper dive site at 90 to 130 feet

hazards.text: Current can make the wreck undiveable at times

summary.text: The Duane's sister cutter, lying on its side in deeper water off Key Largo. It is a deeper, advanced dive, and current can shut it down on some days.

sites.name: Eagle Wreck

s1.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s1.quote: lying on its starboard side in 110 feet of water 3 miles northeast of Alligator Reef Light … The deck railings at 70 feet, and its propeller and rudder at 110 feet, are still intact.

s2.quote: This 287-foot freighter is one of the great places to dive for wreck enthusiasts. Look for massive goliath groupers, bull sharks, and thousands of schooling jacks

highlights.text: Goliath groupers and bull sharks
Schooling jacks around the hull
Propeller and rudder still intact

hazards.text: Wreck broken in half by Hurricane Georges

summary.text: A 287-foot freighter resting on its starboard side off Islamorada, with rails near 70 feet and propeller at 110. Big groupers, bull sharks and jacks circle the wreck.

sites.depthNote: Rails 70 ft, prop and rudder 110 ft

sites.name: Vandenberg Wreck

s1.publisher: Florida Keys & Key West tourism council
s1.quote: the bottom of its hull rests on sand in depths averaging 145 feet, but its superstructure rises to about 45 feet below the surface

s2.quote: The ship offers a solid 100 ft (30 m) of relief with dive profiles for everyone from novice divers to advanced technical and wreck-penetration divers. … rests at a depth of 140 ft (43 m)

highlights.text: About 100 ft of vertical relief

summary.text: A 523-foot former missile-tracking ship sunk off Key West, one of the largest purpose-sunk wrecks anywhere. Its hull sits at about 145 feet while the top reaches 45 feet, so there is a profile for most divers.

sites.depthNote: Superstructure 45 ft, hull on sand about 145 ft

s1.publisher: Key West Dive Center
s1.quote: one of the most popular and well-known novice scuba diving wreck sites … standing proudly on the ocean floor in 65 feet of water … the bow and stern are separated by approximately 30 feet

s2.quote: 65 feet below the surface of the sea … The visibility of the area is usually excellent … a steel-hull shrimper which measures 75 feet in length

highlights.text: Moray eels and schools of fish in the hull
Resident goliath grouper known as Elvis

summary.text: A 75-foot steel shrimp boat, not a tug, lying in two halves in about 65 feet off Key West. A popular novice wreck with schooling fish, morays and often excellent visibility.

s1.publisher: Divers Alert Network

s2.quote: The 210-foot island freighter Adolphus Busch Senior … in 100 feet of water southwest of Big Pine Key

summary.text: A 210-foot freighter standing upright on sand near Looe Key in the Lower Keys, sunk in 1998 as an artificial reef and now part of the Florida Keys shipwreck trail.

highlights.text: Iron mast and hull remains with gorgonians and sponges

summary.text: The scattered remains of a three-masted sailing ship wrecked in 1889, lying in about 20 feet near Duck Key and covered with sponges, gorgonians and corals.
